Additionally, we introduce two novel classes of conformity scores for multi-output regression that generalize their univariate counterparts. These scores ensure asymptotic conditional coverage while maintaining exact finite-sample marginal coverage. One class is compatible with any generative model, offering broad applicability, while the other is computationally efficient, leveraging the properties of invertible generative models. Finally, we conduct a comprehensive empirical evaluation across 13 tabular datasets, comparing all the multi-output conformal methods explored in this work. To ensure a fair and consistent comparison, all methods are implemented within a unified code base.
author: Victor Dheur, Matteo Fontana, Yorick Estievenart, Naomi Desobry, Souhaib Ben Taieb

title: JustLogic: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Deductive Reasoning in Large Language Models
content:
arXiv:2501.14851v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Logical reasoning is a critical component of Large Language Models (LLMs), and substantial research efforts in recent years have aimed to enhance their deductive reasoning abilities. However, existing deductive reasoning benchmarks suffer from significant constraints that restrict their utility, i.e., the lack of task complexity, the presence of prior knowledge as a confounder, and superficial error analysis. To address these deficiencies, we introduce JustLogic, a synthetically generated benchmark for evaluating deduction in propositional logic. Within this fragment, JustLogic is (i) complex, capable of generating a diverse range of linguistic patterns, vocabulary, and argument structures, (ii) prior knowledge independent, substantially reducing the advantage of models possessing prior knowledge so that questions are answerable from the given premises alone, and (iii) capable of in-depth error analysis on the heterogeneous effects of proof size and argument form on model accuracy. Our experimental results on JustLogic reveal that (i) several state-of-the-art (SOTA) reasoning LLMs score above the human average on JustLogic, although only DeepSeek R1's margin is significant on the matched items after correction for multiple comparisons, and (ii) the evaluated non-reasoning models score below the human average. Given the small human study (18 participants, seven questions each), these comparisons are indicative. All code and data are available at https://github.com/michaelchen-lab/JustLogic
author: Michael K. Chen, Xikun Zhang, Yao Li, Dacheng Tao

title: Coresets for Density-Based Clustering via Bayesian Predictive Partition Matching
content:
arXiv:2502.05725v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Density-based clustering identifies groups as connected high-density regions, accommodating irregular shapes and reflecting their geometry, but this reliance on density estimation introduces uncertainty into the resulting partitions, which is often costly to quantify. To represent this uncertainty efficiently, we construct a compact representation of the data, or coreset, designed to preserve the distribution of predictive density-based partitions. We sample observations from a Dirichlet process surrogate, smooth them to estimate densities, and use the resulting level sets to partition a common reference set. Starting from a uniform subsample, we learn an affine transformation that improves agreement with full-data partitions by minimizing a tractable approximation to paired expected variation of information. Fresh, independent predictive simulations then guide the selection of the final transformation. Our analysis provides approximation and selection guarantees and establishes consistency for ideal fixed-resolution partitions under geometric conditions. Simulations and an application to mass cytometry show improved partition agreement over uniform subsampling, often matching substantially larger supports.
author: Bernardo Flores

title: New Lower Bounds for Stochastic Non-Convex Optimization through Divergence Decomposition
content:
arXiv:2502.14060v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study fundamental limits of first-order stochastic optimization in a range of nonconvex settings, including L-smooth functions satisfying Quasar-Convexity (QC), Quadratic Growth (QG), and Restricted Secant Inequalities (RSI). While the convergence properties of standard algorithms are well-understood in deterministic regimes, significantly fewer results address the stochastic case, where only unbiased and noisy gradients are available. We establish new lower bounds on the number of noisy gradient queries to minimize these classes of functions, also showing that they are tight (up to a logarithmic factor) in all the relevant quantities characterizing each class. Our approach reformulates the optimization task as a function identification problem, leveraging divergence decomposition arguments to construct a challenging subclass that leads to sharp lower bounds. Furthermore, we present a specialized algorithm in the one-dimensional setting that achieves faster rates, suggesting that certain dimensional thresholds are intrinsic to the complexity of non-convex stochastic optimization.
author: El Mehdi Saad, Wei-Cheng Lee, Francesco Orabona

title: Mamba-3D as Masked Autoencoders for Accurate and Data-Efficient Analysis of Medical Ultrasound Videos
content:
arXiv:2503.20258v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Ultrasound videos are an important form of clinical imaging data, and deep learning-based automated analysis can improve diagnostic accuracy and clinical efficiency. However, the scarcity of labeled data and the inherent challenges of video analysis have impeded the advancement of related methods. In this work, we introduce E-ViM$^3$, a data-efficient Vision Mamba network that preserves the 3D structure of video data, enhancing long-range dependencies and inductive biases to better model space-time correlations. With our design of Enclosure Global Tokens (EGT), the model captures and aggregates global features more effectively than competing methods. To further improve data efficiency, we employ masked video modeling for self-supervised pre-training, with the proposed Spatial-Temporal Chained (STC) masking strategy designed to adapt to various video scenarios. Experiments demonstrate that E-ViM$^3$ performs as the state-of-the-art in two high-level semantic analysis tasks across four datasets of varying sizes: EchoNet-Dynamic, CAMUS, MICCAI-BUV, and WHBUS. Furthermore, our model achieves competitive performance with limited labels, highlighting its potential impact on real-world clinical applications.
author: Jiaheng Zhou, Yanfeng Zhou, Wei Fang, Yuxing Tang, Le Lu, Ge Yang

title: HierSum: A Global and Local Attention Mechanism for Video Summarization
content:
arXiv:2504.18689v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Video summarization creates an abridged version (i.e., a summary) that provides a quick overview of the video while retaining pertinent information. In this work, we focus on summarizing instructional videos and propose a method for breaking down a video into meaningful segments, each corresponding to essential steps in the video. We propose **HierSum**, a hierarchical approach that integrates fine-grained local cues from subtitles with global contextual information provided by video-level instructions. Our approach utilizes the "most replayed" statistic as a supervisory signal to identify critical segments, thereby improving the effectiveness of the summary. We evaluate on benchmark datasets such as TVSum, BLiSS, Mr.HiSum, and the WikiHow test set, and show that HierSum consistently outperforms existing methods in key metrics such as F1-score and rank correlation. We also curate a new multi-modal dataset using WikiHow and EHow videos, and associated articles containing step-by-step instructions. Through extensive ablation studies, we demonstrate that training on this dataset significantly enhances summarization on the target datasets. The code and dataset will be available at https://github.com/ApoorvaBeedu/HierSum.
author: Apoorva Beedu, Irfan Essa

title: Learning mechanical systems from real-world data using discrete forced Lagrangian dynamics
content:
arXiv:2505.20370v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We introduce a data-driven method for learning the equations of motion of mechanical systems directly from position measurements. This is particularly relevant in system identification tasks where only positional information is available, such as motion capture, pixel data or low-resolution tracking. Our approach takes advantage of the discrete Lagrange-d'Alembert principle and the forced discrete Euler-Lagrange equations to construct a physically grounded model of the system's dynamics. We decompose the dynamics into conservative and non-conservative components, which are learned separately using feed-forward neural networks. In the absence of external forces, our method reduces to a variational discretization of the action principle naturally preserving the symplectic structure of the underlying Hamiltonian system. We validate our approach on a variety of synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to baseline methods. In particular, we apply our model to (1) measured human motion data and (2) latent embeddings obtained via an autoencoder trained on image sequences. We demonstrate that we can faithfully reconstruct and separate both the conservative and forced dynamics, yielding interpretable and physically consistent predictions
author: Martine Dyring Hansen, Elena Celledoni, Benjamin Kwanen Tapley

title: Cross-modal RAG: Sub-dimensional Text-to-Image Retrieval-Augmented Generation
content:
arXiv:2505.21956v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Text-to-image generation increasingly demands access to domain-specific, fine-grained, and rapidly evolving knowledge that pretrained models cannot fully capture, necessitating the integration of retrieval methods. Existing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) methods attempt to address this by retrieving globally relevant images, but they fail when no single image contains all desired elements from a complex user query. We propose Cross-modal RAG, a novel framework that decomposes both queries and images into sub-dimensional components, enabling subquery-aware retrieval and generation. Our method introduces a hybrid retrieval strategy, combining a sub-dimensional sparse retriever with a dense retriever, to identify a Pareto-optimal set of images, each contributing complementary aspects of the query. During generation, a multimodal large language model is guided to selectively condition on relevant visual features aligned to specific subqueries for subquery-aware image synthesis. Extensive experiments on MS-COCO, Flickr30K, WikiArt, CUB, and ImageNet-LT demonstrate that Cross-modal RAG significantly outperforms existing baselines in the retrieval and further contributes to generation quality, while maintaining high efficiency.
author: Mengdan Zhu, Senhao Cheng, Guangji Bai, Yifei Zhang, Liang Zhao

title: Distribution free M-estimation
content:
arXiv:2505.22807v5 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The basic question of delineating those statistical problems that are solvable without making any assumptions on the underlying data distribution has long animated statistics and learning theory. This paper characterizes when a convex M-estimation or stochastic optimization problem is solvable in such an assumption-free setting, providing a precise dividing line between solvable and unsolvable problems. The conditions we identify show, perhaps surprisingly, that Lipschitz continuity of the loss being minimized is not necessary for distribution free minimization, and they are also distinct from classical characterizations of learnability in machine learning.
author: Felipe Areces, John C. Duchi

title: Resource-Efficient Quantum Reinforcement Learning on NISQ Devices with Dynamic-Circuit Qubit Reuse and Grover-Based Trajectory Search
content:
arXiv:2509.16002v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: A resource-efficient quantum reinforcement learning framework for finite-horizon quantum Markov decision processes is presented, employing dynamic-circuit qubit reuse to reduce the interaction-workspace requirements of multi-step execution. The framework integrates quantum state-transition and reward encoding, dynamic-circuit execution, quantum return evaluation, and Grover-based trajectory search. Its central contribution is a dynamic execution model in which a fixed interaction workspace is reused across sequential agent-environment interactions through mid-circuit measurement, qubit reset, and next-state propagation. For the considered benchmark, this approach reduces the interaction-workspace requirement from 7T qubits under a static circuit to a constant seven qubits, independent of the interaction horizon T. This corresponds to a 66% reduction for the three-step benchmark and transforms the interaction-workspace complexity from O(T) to O(1). Trajectory returns are evaluated using reversible quantum arithmetic, and Grover's algorithm identifies the optimal trajectories, so that return evaluation and trajectory search are performed within a unified quantum-native pipeline. Ideal simulations demonstrate that the dynamic implementation preserves the valid trajectory structure of the static formulation, with quantitative comparisons assessing the agreement between their trajectory distributions. Finally, execution on an IBM Heron-class processor demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed dynamic-circuit architecture on noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware.
author: Thet Htar Su, Shaswot Shresthamali, Masaaki Kondo

title: Two Heads Are Better Than One: Audio-Visual Speech Error Correction with Dual Hypotheses
content:
arXiv:2510.13281v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: This paper introduces a new paradigm for generative error correction (GER) framework in audio-visual speech recognition (AVSR) that reasons over modality-specific evidences directly in the language space. Our framework, DualHyp, empowers a large language model (LLM) to compose independent N-best hypotheses from separate automatic speech recognition (ASR) and visual speech recognition (VSR) models. To maximize the effectiveness of DualHyp, we further introduce RelPrompt, a noise-aware guidance mechanism that provides modality-grounded prompts to the LLM. RelPrompt offers the temporal reliability of each modality stream, guiding the model to dynamically switch its focus between ASR and VSR hypotheses for an accurate correction. Under various corruption scenarios, our framework attains up to 57.7% error rate gain on the LRS2 benchmark over standard ASR baseline, contrary to single-stream GER approaches that achieve only 10% gain. To facilitate research within our DualHyp framework, we release the code and the dataset comprising ASR and VSR hypotheses at https://github.com/sungnyun/dualhyp.
author: Sungnyun Kim, Kangwook Jang, Sungwoo Cho, Joon Son Chung, Hoirin Kim, Se-Young Yun

title: Fault Detection in Solar Thermal Systems using Probabilistic Reconstructions
content:
arXiv:2511.10296v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Solar thermal systems (STS) present a promising avenue for low-carbon heat generation, with a well-running system providing heat at minimal cost and carbon emissions. However, STS can exhibit faults due to improper installation, maintenance, or operation, often resulting in a substantial reduction in efficiency or even damage to the system. As monitoring at the individual level is economically prohibitive for small-scale systems, automated monitoring and fault detection should be used to address such issues. Recent advances in data-driven anomaly detection, particularly in time series analysis, offer a cost-effective solution by leveraging existing sensors to identify abnormal system states. Here, we apply probabilistic reconstruction-based anomaly detection to the publicly available PaSTS dataset of operational domestic STS, which features real-world complexities and diverse fault types. We combine an LSTM-based Variational Autoencoder with heteroscedastic uncertainty estimation and evaluate it exclusively on systems unseen during training. Our experiments show that reconstruction-based methods detect faults in domestic STS both qualitatively and quantitatively. Our model achieves the best generalisation to unseen systems among all evaluated methods, while a rescaled PCA reconstruction baseline remains competitive on pooled threshold-free metrics. An ablation shows that heteroscedastic uncertainty estimation drives the gain in cross-system generalisation. Finally, we discuss the engineering overhead required to unlock these improvements and make a case for simple deep learning models.
author: Florian Ebmeier, Nicole Ludwig, Jannik Thuemmel, Georg Martius, Volker H. Franz

title: Understanding temperature tuning in energy-based models
content:
arXiv:2512.09152v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Generative models of complex systems often require post hoc parameter adjustments to produce useful outputs. For example, energy-based models for protein design are sampled at an artificially low "temperature" to generate novel, functional sequences. This temperature tuning is a common yet poorly understood heuristic used across machine learning contexts to control the trade-off between generative fidelity and diversity. Here, we develop an interpretable, physically motivated framework to explain this phenomenon. We demonstrate that in systems with a large "energy gap" separating a small fraction of meaningful states from a vast space of unrealistic states, learning from sparse data causes models to systematically overestimate high-energy state probabilities, a bias that lowering the sampling temperature corrects. More generally, we characterize how the optimal sampling temperature depends on the interplay between data size and the system's underlying energy landscape, and that this interplay is sufficient to elicit the tuning phenomenon; regularizing while training can contribute, but is not necessary. Crucially, our results show that lowering the sampling temperature is not always desirable. We identify the conditions under which raising it results in better generative performance. Our framework reveals that post hoc temperature tuning is indicative of both specific properties of the true data distribution and the limits of the learned model due to insufficient data availability.
author: Peter W Fields, Vudtiwat Ngampruetikorn, David J Schwab, Stephanie E Palmer

title: Graph-based Nearest Neighbors with Dynamic Updates via Random Walks
content:
arXiv:2512.18060v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANN) is a common way to retrieve relevant search results, especially now in the context of large language models and retrieval augmented generation. One of the most widely used algorithms for ANN is based on constructing a multi-layer graph over the dataset, called the Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW). While this algorithm supports insertion of new data, it does not support deletion of existing data. Moreover, deletion algorithms described by prior work come at the cost of increased query latency, decreased recall, or prolonged deletion time. In this paper, we propose a new theoretical framework for graph-based ANN based on random walks. We then utilize this framework to analyze a randomized deletion approach that approximately preserves hitting time statistics compared to the graph before deleting the point. However, this guarantee needs at least as many edge samples as there are edges in the clique over the neighbors of the deleted point. We then turn this theoretical framework into a deterministic deletion algorithm, and show that it provides a better tradeoff between query latency, recall, deletion time, and memory usage through an extensive collection of experiments.
author: Nina Mishra, Yonatan Naamad, Tal Wagner, Lichen Zhang

title: HyperCLOVA X 32B Think
content:
arXiv:2601.03286v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: In this report, we present HyperCLOVA X 32B Think, a vision-language model designed with particular emphasis on reasoning within the Korean linguistic and cultural context, as well as agentic ability. HyperCLOVA X 32B Think is pre-trained with a strong focus on reasoning capabilities and subsequently post-trained to support multimodal understanding, enhanced reasoning, agentic behaviors, and alignment with human preferences. Experimental evaluations against comparably sized models demonstrate that our model achieves strong performance on Korean text-to-text and vision-to-text benchmarks, as well as on agent-oriented evaluation tasks. By open-sourcing HyperCLOVA X 32B Think, we aim to support broader adoption and facilitate further research and innovation across both academic and industrial communities.
author: NAVER Cloud HyperCLOVA X Team

title: Stochastic Deep Learning: A Probabilistic Framework for Modeling Uncertainty in Structured Temporal Data
content:
arXiv:2601.05227v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: I propose a novel framework that integrates stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with deep generative models to improve uncertainty quantification in machine learning applications involving structured and temporal data. This approach, termed Stochastic Latent Differential Inference (SLDI), embeds an It\^o SDE in the latent space of a variational autoencoder, allowing for flexible, continuous-time modeling of uncertainty while preserving a principled mathematical foundation. The drift and diffusion terms of the SDE are parameterized by neural networks, enabling data-driven inference and generalizing classical time series models to handle irregular sampling and complex dynamic structure.
  A central theoretical contribution is the co-parameterization of the adjoint state with a dedicated neural network, forming a coupled forward-backward system that captures not only latent evolution but also gradient dynamics. I introduce a pathwise-regularized adjoint loss and analyze variance-reduced gradient flows through the lens of stochastic calculus, offering new tools for improving training stability in deep latent SDEs. My paper unifies and extends variational inference, continuous-time generative modeling, and control-theoretic optimization, providing a rigorous foundation for future developments in stochastic probabilistic machine learning.
author: James Rice

title: Sublinear Time Quantum Algorithm for Attention Approximation
content:
arXiv:2602.00874v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Given the query, key and value matrices $Q, K, V\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, the attention module is defined as $\mathrm{Att}(Q, K, V)=D^{-1}AV$ where $A=\exp(QK^\top/\sqrt{d})$ with $\exp(\cdot)$ applied entrywise, $D=\mathrm{diag}(A\mathbf{1}_n)$. The attention module is the backbone of modern transformers and large language models, but explicitly forming the softmax matrix $D^{-1}A$ incurs $\Omega(n^2)$ time, motivating numerous approximation schemes that reduce runtime to $\widetilde O(nd)$ via sparsity or low-rank factorization.
  We propose a quantum data structure that approximates any row of $\mathrm{Att}(Q, K, V)$ using only row queries to $Q, K, V$. Our algorithm preprocesses these matrices in $\widetilde{O}(\epsilon^{-1} n^{0.5} (s_\lambda^{3} + s_\lambda^{2} d + d) + \epsilon^{-2} s_\lambda d)$ time, where $\epsilon$ is the target accuracy and $s_\lambda$ is the $\lambda$-statistical dimension of the exponential kernel defined by $Q$ and $K$. Each row query can be answered in $\widetilde{O}(s_\lambda^2 + s_\lambda d)$ time. If every row sum of $A$ exceeds $\epsilon\|A\|+\lambda\sqrt n$, then with probability $1-1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ the answers have Frobenius-norm error $O(\beta\|D^{-1}\|(\epsilon\|A\|_F+\lambda\sqrt n)\|V\|_F)$. Here $\beta=(1-(\epsilon\|A\|+\lambda\sqrt n)\|D^{-1}\|)^{-1}\geq 1$ is close to $1$ when every row sum is much larger than $\epsilon\|A\|+\lambda\sqrt n$.
  To our knowledge, this is the first quantum data structure that approximates rows of the attention matrix in sublinear time with respect to $n$. Our approach relies on a quantum Nystr\"om approximation of the exponential kernel, quantum multivariate mean estimation for computing $D$, and quantum sampling of the rows of $V$ by their squared norms, with a median over independent samples, for the multiplication with $V$.
author: Zhao Song, Jianfei Xue, Jiahao Zhang, Lichen Zhang

title: How much perceived-stress signal is in the maternal ECG? An exclusion bound across deep-learning and heart-rate-variability representations in pregnancy
content:
arXiv:2602.03886v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Deep learning can read physiological states from the electrocardiogram (ECG), prompting attempts to detect psychological stress. We asked how much information about perceived stress the maternal ECG carries. In 144 pregnant women, with every cross-validation split taken over participants, across 94 arms spanning 21 self-supervised, foundation-model, and heart-rate-variability architectures, the best discrimination of moderate-to-high stress (PSS-10 >= 19) was AUC 0.604 (95% CI 0.511-0.696), and AUC >= 0.70 was rejected in all eleven arms tested. Three pre-registered tests in a second cohort from the same center, recorded on different hardware, were null, at 30% power. Which of the three simultaneously recorded ECG channels was analyzed accounted for 96% of the predicted score's variance, against 4% between women; across 20 combinations of channel rule, label variant, and visit, the external correlation with perceived stress ranged from r = -0.095 to r = +0.307, a spread no larger than such a search produces by chance (raw one-sided p of the maximum 0.011; calibrated max-statistic p = 0.583). Hair cortisol was not predicted either. In the second cohort, PSS-10 scores were not stable across administrations spanning pregnancy and the postpartum period (ICC 0.06-0.16), so one administration is a weak measure of a woman's stress level at another visit. A single-recording ECG screener for perceived stress is excluded in this population, and multi-channel studies must pre-register their channel rule.
author: Martin G. Frasch, Marlene J. E. Mayer, Clara Becker, Peter Zimmermann, Camilla Zelgert, Nicolas B. Garnier, Marta C. Antonelli, Silvia M. Lobmaier

title: On the Meta-Design of Allocation Problems
content:
arXiv:2602.08786v5 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: There is an extensive literature that studies how to find optimal policies in resource allocation problems, taking the underlying design parameters that define the allocation, such as what data is collected, how many people can be served, and quality of service as fixed constraints. Yet, from a planner's perspective, these design parameters are themselves optimization variables that are just as important in determining overall welfare as selecting the optimal targeting rule for a given set of constraints. This realization motivates a rich set of meta-design questions exploring how planners should make principled decisions about investments in prediction, capacity constraints, and treatment quality, all of which lie upstream of classical policy optimization. Building on initial theoretical work in this space, our paper has three main contributions. First, we formally define the broad meta-design space of resource allocation problems. Second, we develop empirical tools that enable practitioners to reliably navigate it. Third, we demonstrate the framework in two real-world case studies on German employment services and targeted cash transfer programs in Ethiopia.
author: Unai Fischer-Abaigar, Emily Aiken, Christoph Kern, Juan Carlos Perdomo

title: Neural Learning of Fast Matrix Multiplication Algorithms: a Geometric Perspective
content:
arXiv:2602.21797v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We combine neural learning and geometric diagnostics to investigate the rank and border rank of the \(3\times3\) matrix-multiplication tensor \(M_3\). Using the Bhattacharya--Mesner product, we derive \textsc{MatMulNet}, a differentiable architecture encoding bilinear maps. Constrained refinement yields a length-\(23\) numerical solution with machine-precision full-tensor residual and bounded decomposition weight. Along the explored length-\(22\) branch, the residual instead decreases as the gauge-invariant weight grows. This contrast supports \(R_{\mathbb R}(M_3)=23\) as a working hypothesis. A Laurent-parametrised extension probes border rank, giving a tentative, protocol-dependent motivation to investigate \(r=19\) and the adjacent \(r=18\) case. For \(M_4\), the same diagnostics distinguish bounded numerical solutions recovered from perturbed known schemes, structured residual plateaus, and weight-growing approximations, revealing the dependence of the search on initialisation. Together, the experiments connect approximation accuracy with decomposition growth and identify concrete targets for exact or certified investigation.
author: Paolo Andreini, Alessandra Bernardi, Monica Bianchini, Barbara Toniella Corradini, Sara Marziali, Giacomo Nunziati, Franco Scarselli

title: A Trust-Region Interior-Point Stochastic Sequential Quadratic Programming Method
content:
arXiv:2603.10230v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a trust-region interior-point stochastic sequential quadratic programming (TR-IP-SSQP) method for solving optimization problems with a stochastic objective and deterministic nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. In this setting, exact evaluations of the objective function and its gradient are unavailable, but their stochastic estimates can be constructed. In particular, at each iteration our method builds stochastic oracles whose estimates of the objective value and gradient satisfy proper adaptive accuracy conditions with a fixed probability. To handle inequality constraints, we adopt an interior-point method (IPM), in which the barrier parameter is taken from a prescribed decreasing sequence and is reduced once a stochastic stationarity test is passed. Under standard assumptions, we show that, almost surely, the KKT residual vanishes along the iterations at which the barrier parameter is reduced, and every limit point of these iterates is a KKT point. We implement the method on a subset of problems from the CUTEst test set, as well as on constrained logistic regression problems, to demonstrate its practical performance.
author: Yuchen Fang, Jihun Kim, Sen Na, James Demmel, Javad Lavaei

title: Measuring AI Agents' Progress on Multi-Step Cyber Attack Scenarios
content:
arXiv:2603.11214v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We evaluate the autonomous offensive cyber capabilities of frontier AI agents on two purpose-built cyber ranges---a 32-step corporate network attack and a 7-step industrial control system attack targeting a simulated cooling tower---complemented by a private 76-task CTF suite spanning four difficulty tiers. Human-expert solve times are estimated at roughly 20 hours for the corporate range and 15 hours for the cooling tower; CTF time annotations range from 1 minute to over 42 hours and include measured playtests, designer estimates, and lower bounds from unsolved playtests. Across thirteen models released over a twenty-month period---from GPT-4o in August 2024 to GPT-5.5 in April 2026---we observe two trends. First, step-count progress increases approximately log-linearly with inference-time compute over the tested range (up to 100M tokens). Second, newer frontier models generally complete more steps at fixed token budgets. GPT-5.5 and Mythos Glasswing each completed all 32 steps in at least one run, the first end-to-end completions of the corporate range; Mythos Glasswing averaged 25.2 of 32 steps and completed the chain in 6 of 10 runs, and GPT-5.5 averaged 22.3 and completed it in 2 of 10. On the control system range, Mythos Glasswing achieved the first end-to-end completion of the chain (2 of 10 runs, mean 4.2); the other frontier models reached at most 3 of 7 steps by directly probing the operational-technology protocol rather than following the intended chain of IT compromise and authenticated control. These results indicate rapid improvements in autonomous cyber capability and suggest that complex but undefended multi-step ranges---including industrial-control attack chains---are no longer reliably distinguishing the strongest frontier models. Future evaluations should emphasise hardened environments, active defences, defensive-control effectiveness, and operational security.
author: Linus Folkerts, Will Payne, Simon Inman, Philippos Giavridis, Joe Skinner, Sam Deverett, James Aung, Ekin Zorer, Michael Schmatz, Mahmoud Ghanem, John Wilkinson, Alan Steer, Vy Hong, Harry Coppock, Jessica Wang

title: How to find expressible and trainable parameterized quantum circuits?
content:
arXiv:2603.14451v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Whether parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs) can be systematically constructed to be both trainable and expressive remains an open question. Highly expressive PQCs often exhibit barren plateaus, while several trainable alternatives admit efficient classical simulation. We prove that deciding whether a PQC family exhibits a barren plateau is undecidable in general. However, we derive a practical finite-sample, dimension-independent concentration bound for estimating the variance of a PQC cost function, yielding explicit trainability guarantees. Across commonly used ans\"atze, we observe an anticorrelation between trainability and expressibility, consistent with theoretical insights. Building on this observation, we propose a property-based ansatz-search framework for identifying circuits that combine trainability and expressibility. We demonstrate its practical viability on a real quantum computer and apply it to variational quantum algorithms. We identify quantum neural network ans\"atze with improved effective dimension using over six times fewer parameters, and for VQE on $\mathrm{H}_2$ we achieve UCCSD-like accuracy at substantially reduced circuit complexity.
author: Peter R\"oseler, Dennis Willsch, Kristel Michielsen

title: One-sided certification of surrogate near-minimizers: exact worst-case envelopes under strong convexity and smoothness
content:
arXiv:2604.05678v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study target suboptimality for points that approximately minimize a surrogate objective. Unlike standard uniform perturbation estimates, the available comparison is one-sided, thresholded at a certified lower target level, and restricted to the entire surrogate-selected sublevel set. We first show that selected comparison alone cannot yield a finite worst-case guarantee, even for strongly convex quadratics with identical Hessians. A single scalar upper bound on the surrogate minimum closes this information gap and leads to a sharp general estimate. For pairs of $\mu$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth objectives, we then solve the associated worst-case information problem exactly. We obtain a sharp feasibility barrier and a dimension-free envelope; in its nontrivial regime, the value reduces to a scalar maximization over a compact interval. Explicit one-dimensional piecewise-quadratic objectives attain the bound while satisfying the one-sided constraint on the full selected set. We characterize when curvature strictly improves the general certificate and provide a threshold-preserving finite-net validation procedure. The results identify the best guarantee permitted by the prescribed partial information, independently of any particular optimization algorithm or additive perturbation model.
author: Karim Bounja, Boujema\^a Achchab, Abdeljalil Sakat

title: On Higher-Order Geometric Refinements of Classical Covariance Asymptotics: An Approach via Intrinsic and Extrinsic Information Geometry
content:
arXiv:2604.12725v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Classical Fisher-information asymptotics describe the covariance of regular efficient estimators through the local quadratic approximation of the log-likelihood, and thus capture first-order geometry only. In curved models, including mixtures, curved exponential families, latent-variable models, and manifold-constrained parameter spaces, finite-sample behavior can deviate systematically from these predictions. We develop a coordinate-invariant, curvature-aware refinement by viewing a regular parametric family as a Riemannian manifold \((\Theta,g)\) with Fisher--Rao metric, immersed in \(L^2(\mu)\) through the square-root density map. Under suitable regularity and moment assumptions, we derive an \(n^{-2}\) correction to the leading \(n^{-1}I(\theta)^{-1}\) covariance term for score-root, first-order efficient estimators. The correction is governed by a tensor \(P_{ij}\) that decomposes canonically into three parts, an intrinsic Ricci-type contraction of the Fisher--Rao curvature tensor, an extrinsic Gram-type contraction of the second fundamental form, and a Hellinger discrepancy tensor encoding higher-order probabilistic information not determined by immersion geometry alone. The extrinsic term is positive semidefinite, the full correction is invariant under smooth reparameterization, and it vanishes identically for full exponential families. We then extend the picture to singular models, where Fisher information degenerates. Using resolution of singularities under an additive normal crossing assumption, we describe the resolved metric, the role of the real log canonical threshold in learning rates and posterior mean-squared error, and a curvature-based covariance expansion on the resolved space that recovers the regular theory as a special case. This framework also suggests geometric diagnostics of weak identifiability and curvature-aware principles for regularization and optimization.
author: Malik Amir, Sourangshu Ghosh

title: Well-Conditioned Oblivious Perturbations in Linear Space
content:
arXiv:2604.23193v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Perturbing a deterministic $n$-dimensional matrix with small Gaussian noise is a cornerstone of smoothed analysis of algorithms [Spielman and Teng, JACM 2004], as it reduces the condition number of the input to $O(n)$, and with it the complexity of many matrix algorithms. However, when deployed algorithmically, these perturbations are expensive due to the cost of generating and storing $n^2$ Gaussian random variables. We propose a perturbation that requires generating and storing $O(n)$ random numbers in $O(\log n)$ bits of precision, and reduces the condition number of any deterministic matrix to $O(n)$, matching Gaussian perturbations. Our result takes a step towards derandomizing matrix perturbations in numerical linear algebra, and in particular, implies that we can solve an $n\times n$ linear system to within $\varepsilon$ backward error in $O(n^2\log(n)/\varepsilon)$ time using only $O(n\log n)$ random bits.
  In our construction, we introduce the concept of a pattern matrix, which is a dense deterministic matrix that maps all sparse vectors into dense vectors in a way that goes beyond the classical uncertainty principle of the Fourier transform. We combine this with a sparse perturbation whose entries are dependent and located in a non-uniform fashion. In order to analyze this construction, we develop new techniques for lower bounding the smallest singular value of a random matrix with dependent entries.
author: Shabarish Chenakkod, Micha{\l} Derezi\'nski, Xiaoyu Dong, Mark Rudelson

title: RealICU: Do LLM Agents Understand Long-Context ICU Data? A Benchmark Beyond Behavior Imitation
content:
arXiv:2605.13542v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Intensive care units (ICU) generate long, dense and evolving streams of clinical information, where physicians must repeatedly reassess patient states under time pressure, underscoring a clear need for reliable AI decision support. Existing ICU benchmarks typically treat historical clinician actions as ground truth. However, these actions are made under incomplete information and limited temporal context of the underlying patient state, and may therefore be suboptimal, making it difficult to assess the true reasoning capabilities of AI systems. We introduce RealICU, a hindsight-annotated benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) under realistic ICU conditions, where labels are created after senior physicians review the full patient trajectory. We formulate four physician-motivated tasks: assess Patient Status, Acute Problems, Recommended Actions, and Red Flag actions that risk unsafe outcomes. We partition each trajectory with 30-min windows and release two datasets: RealICU-Gold with 930-window annotations from 94 MIMIC-IV patients, and RealICU-Scale with 11,862 windows extended by Oracle, a physician-validated LLM hindsight labeler. Existing LLMs including memory-augmented ones performed poorly on RealICU, exposing two failure modes: a recall-safety tradeoff for clinical recommendations, and an anchoring bias to early interpretations of the patient. We further introduce ICU-Evo to study structured-memory agents that improves long-horizon reasoning but does not fully eliminate safety failures. Together, RealICU provides a clinically grounded testbed for measuring and improving AI sequential decision-support in high-stakes care. Project page: https://chengzhi-leo.github.io/RealICU-Bench/
author: Chengzhi Shen (Cherise), Weixiang Shen (Cherise), Tobias Susetzky (Cherise),  Chen (Cherise),  Chen (Cherise), Jun Li, Yuyuan Liu, Xuepeng Zhang, Zhenyu Gong, Daniel Rueckert, Jiazhen Pan

title: To See is Not to Learn: Protecting Multimodal Data from Unauthorized Fine-Tuning of Large Vision-Language Models
content:
arXiv:2605.14291v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) is increasingly accompanied by unauthorized scraping and training on multimodal web data, posing copyright and privacy risks to data owners. Existing countermeasures, such as machine unlearning and watermarks, are inherently post-hoc approaches that act only after intellectual property infringement has already occurred. In this work, we propose MMGuard to empower data owners to proactively protect their multimodal data against unauthorized LVLM fine-tuning. MMGuard generates unlearnable examples by injecting human-imperceptible perturbations that exploit the learning dynamics of LVLMs. By minimizing the training loss, the perturbation creates an optimization shortcut, causing the model to overfit to the noise and thereby degrading downstream performance when the perturbation is absent during inference. To further strengthen this defense, MMGuard introduces a cross-modal binding disruption, shifting LVLM attention to enforce a spurious correlation between the noise and the training target with theoretical guarantees. MMGuard is evaluated against nine open-source LVLMs across six datasets. Our results demonstrate effective, stealthy, and robust protection under white-box, gray-box, and no-box threat models, establishing a mechanistic advantage in proactively defending against unauthorized fine-tuning exploitation.
author: Chengshuai Zhao, Zhen Tan, Dawei Li, Tianlong Chen, Zhiyuan Yu, Neil Zhenqiang Gong, Huan Liu

title: Fair outputs, Biased Internals: Causal Potency and Asymmetry of Latent Bias in LLMs for High-Stakes Decisions
content:
arXiv:2605.15217v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Instruction-tuned language models exhibit behavioural fairness in high-stakes decisions while retaining biased associations in their internal representations. However, whether these suppressed representations can affect model outputs - and whether such causal potency is symmetric across demographic groups - remains unknown. We investigate the use of open-weight models for mortgage underwriting using matched applications that differ only in racially-associated names and reveal a critical disconnect: models show no output-level bias, yet retain and amplify demographic representations across model layers. Through activation steering and novel cross-layer interventions, we demonstrate that this suppressed information is decision-relevant: when reinjected at critical layers, it produces near-complete decision reversals. Critically, this latent bias is asymmetric - steering interventions affect decisions in one demographic direction, while producing minimal effects in reverse - and susceptible to adversarial prompt engineering and parameter-efficient fine-tuning. These findings demonstrate that behavioural audits focused on outputs are insufficient: fair outputs can mask exploitable internal biases. They also motivate dual-layer testing frameworks combining output evaluation with representational analysis for AI governance in high-stakes decisions.
author: Jagdish Tripathy, Marcus Buckmann

title: Belief Engine: Making Agent Stance Auditable in LLM Deliberation
content:
arXiv:2605.15343v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: LLM-based AI agents are increasingly used to simulate deliberative social interactions, including negotiation, conflict resolution, and multi-turn opinion exchanges. Simulating human-like opinion change calls for agents that balance existing beliefs with openness to new evidence, while making their responses to that evidence traceable. Current systems often make this difficult: agents may drift from assigned roles, echo an interaction partner, keep a stance despite contrary evidence, or appear to change because the prompt or retrieved context has changed. We introduce the Belief Engine (BE), a framework that uses "belief" in a Bayesian modelling sense, as a maintained evidential state over a proposition that is exposed as a scalar stance. BE extracts structured evidence, stores argument records, and updates the belief state through a Bayesian-inspired stance update in log-odds space with two interpretable controls: evidence uptake u and prior anchoring a. Across multiple LLM models, sweeps of u and a demonstrate stable control over stance dynamics. Higher uptake makes agents more responsive to new evidence, while stronger anchoring preserves the initial stance. On DEBATE, a human deliberation dataset with pre/post opinions, BE is most accurate when participants move in the direction of extracted evidence, showing its strength in evidence-following deliberative contexts. When all participants are evaluated together, gains are more modest because many people remain stable or move for reasons not captured by the extracted evidence stream. BE provides a configurable and auditable belief-update layer for evidence-grounded deliberation, in which LLM agents can be configured as open-minded, anchored, or evidence-sensitive, while their stance trajectories and memory can be audited, compared, and calibrated against human opinion change.
author: Joshua C. Yang, Maurice Flechtner, Damian Dailisan, Michiel A. Bakker

title: Learning-Augmented Online Minimization with Dual Predictions
content:
arXiv:2606.05380v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We present learning-augmented algorithms for two general classes of online minimization problems: metrical task systems and laminar set cover. Both algorithms achieve improved theoretical guarantees using machine-learned predictions of an optimal solution to the dual linear program. Unlike optimal primal solutions, which can change drastically under tiny instance perturbations, these dual solutions are much more stable, which ensures the existence of good (and learnable) predictions for families of similar instances. While previous work has used dual predictions in offline settings and for online maximization problems, our algorithms are, to the best of our knowledge, the first demonstration that such dual predictions can be effective for online minimization. Our theoretical results are complemented by experiments on the $k$-server problem and the parking permit problem.
author: Christian Coester, Alexa Tudose, Alexander Turoczy

title: Boosting Brain-to-Image Decoding with TRIBE v2 Data Augmentation
content:
arXiv:2606.06345v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Brain decoding is limited by the availability of labeled neural data, and remains challenging in low-data regimes. To address this issue, we investigate whether and when brain decoding can be boosted by augmenting small fMRI datasets with synthetic data generated by a pretrained model of fMRI responses to stimuli. We use TRIBE v2, a large encoding model pretrained on more than 1000 hours of fMRI responses to video, audio and language. For each dataset, we evaluate systematic grids that show how the performance of image decoders varies with the amount of synthetic data used for training. Our results, based on two datasets (the 7T fMRI Natural Scenes Dataset and 3T fMRI BOLD5000), show up to 68% improvement in Top-10 image-retrieval accuracy compared to decoders trained only on real data. Importantly, the proportion of augmented data required to reach a given image decoding performance needs to be adjusted depending on the data source. Surprisingly, image decoders trained exclusively on synthetic fMRI can perform above chance in some settings, suggesting that TRIBE v2 can support zero-shot brain-to-image decoding. Together, these results show how large-scale models of the fMRI responses to sight, sound and language may provide a foundation to improve the data efficiency for image decoding.
author: Yohann Benchetrit, Marl\`ene Careil, Simon Dahan, Hubert Banville, St\'ephane d'Ascoli, Jean-R\'emi King

title: From Inference to Adaptation: Vision-Language Model Test-Time Adaptation via a Unified Optimal Transport View
content:
arXiv:2608.18339v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable zero-shot capabilities yet remain sensitive to real-world distribution shifts. Although significant efforts are devoted to adapting VLMs at test time, they rely heavily on noisy pseudo-labels predicted from cross-modal embedding similarities during inference, which are unreliable under distribution shifts and mislead the adaptation. Moreover, existing methods largely overlook the critical relational structures across different modalities during test-time adaptation, whose supervision signals remain surprisingly robust under distribution shifts. In this work, we aim to jointly align the cross-modal semantics and intra-modal relational structures across modalities at test time to improve VLM adaptation. At the inference stage, we formulate the zero-shot image classification task as a cross-modal alignment problem via a Fused Gromov-Wasserstein (FGW) formulation, which considers both cross-modal semantics and intra-modal structures to generate robust pseudo-labels. At the adaptation stage, we propose a multi-level InfoNCE loss to leverage both the semantical and relational alignment supervision from the inference stage, empowering fine-grained adaptation of VLMs under distribution shifts with additional structural consistency. Finally, we bridge the inference and adaptation stages of our method by proving a mathematical equivalence between their objective functions, thereby revealing the mutual benefits of these two stages from a theoretical perspective. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our methods, outperforming the best-performing methods by up to 3% while maintaining a superior balance between effectiveness and efficiency.
author: Qi Yu, Zhichen Zeng, Katherine Tieu, Lingjie Chen, Xiyuan Yang, Ruizhong Qiu, Yuchen Yan, Lihui Liu, Yanjun Zhao, Ziao Wang, Lei Ying, Jingrui He, Hanghang Tong

title: A Single-Loop, Constant-Batch First-Order Penalty Method for Stochastic Bilevel Optimization
content:
arXiv:2610.07290v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Recent advances in penalty-based methods for stochastic bilevel optimization (SBO) have eliminated the need for second-order derivative oracles. However, for stochastic nonconvex-strongly convex bilevel problems, existing first-order methods typically rely on nested loops and/or large batch sizes for attaining $O(\epsilon^{-6})$ or $O(\epsilon^{-4})$ sample complexity under standard bounded-variance assumption or mean-square smoothness assumption. Achieving these rates with a single-loop penalty method and a constant batch size remains challenging due to a large penalty value needed for an accurate approximation. To address this challenge, we develop a stochastic SIngle-loop COnstant-Batch first-order penalty method (SICO) that combines two complementary ingredients. First, it performs one stochastic-gradient update per-iteration for both the original lower-level and penalized problems, with a projection that controls the separation between their iterates. Second, it applies an exponential moving average to stabilize the upper-level gradient estimator. We show that this combination achieves $ O(\epsilon^{-6}) $ sample complexity using only $O(1)$ stochastic-gradient samples per iteration under unbiased, bounded-variance stochastic gradients. Under the additional mean-square smoothness assumption on the lower-level stochastic gradients, the same algorithm improves the complexity to $O(\epsilon^{-4})$ also with $O(1)$ batch size. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to match the best-known convergence rate for fully first-order SBO methods using a single loop and a constant batch size. This result addresses an open problem posed in the literature.
author: Xingyu Chen, Ming Yang, Quanqi Hu, Tianbao Yang

title: From Fusion to Guidance: Physics-Guided Fusion Adaptive Prompting Network for Underwater Semantic Segmentation
content: Semantic segmentation enables pixel-level scene understanding, addressing the increasingly crucial need for accurate underwater scene parsing in marine exploration. The conventional methods underperform in cases of underwater image degradation by turbidity and light attenuation, whereas terrestrial multimodal fusion lacks physics-aware feature discrimination. As a foundational vision model trained on large-scale natural images, segment anything model 2 (SAM2) has demonstrated excellent performance across numerous domains. Although SAM2 provides prompt encoders, its interactive prompting mechanism is unsuited for deep multimodal learning. To address this challenge, a feature learning framework—the physics-guided fusion adaptive prompting network (PAPNet)—was proposed and investigated in this study. Specifically, an underwater semantic segmentation adapter was designed to activate frozen SAM2 backbone networks. Additionally, a Jaffe–McGlamery–DepthSynth fusion module was introduced for the physics-guided fusion of red, green, blue (RGB) and depth images using the classical Jaffe–McGlamery underwater-imaging model. The resulting saliency-adaptive point sampler (SAPS) module adaptively generates training-time point prompts from existing pixel-level labels, thereby avoiding additional manual point-prompt design for prompt learning. The proposed network experimentally improves the fusion of underwater RGB and depth information, suppressing color shifts and blurring artifacts through prompt learning, thereby achieving enhanced pixel-level semantic comprehension in complex underwater environments. Empirical assessments conducted on the benchmark segmentation of underwater imagery (SUIM) dataset confirmed that the proposed approach surpassed existing state-of-the-art benchmarks. PAPNet attained a 77.05% mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) and an 88.32% mean accuracy for underwater semantic segmentation, demonstrating significant advantages over existing methods and setting new benchmarks. The experimental results and network code can be accessed at https://github.com/OntheUnbeli/PAPNet
author: Wujie Zhou, Yu Zheng, Xiaohong Qian, Jiajun Meng, Yuanyuan Liu

title: GlaTMNet: A Universal Frequency-Aware State Space Model for High-Precision Glacier Mapping
content: Glaciers serve as critical indicators of climate change and as major natural freshwater reservoirs. High-precision glacier mapping is essential for assessing the climate impacts and safeguarding water resources. However, accurate glacier mapping remains challenging in complex mountainous environments. The presence of supraglacial debris, seasonal snow, glacial lakes, and floating thin ice severely complicates glacier identification, thereby significantly degrading mapping accuracy. In addition, existing deep learning approaches often generalize poorly across heterogeneous topography and multisource satellite imagery. This vulnerability primarily arises because they overrely on localized spatial features while underusing informative frequency-domain representations and failing to model the long-range spatial dependencies needed for robust, transferable feature extraction. To address these limitations, we propose a Glacier Twin-Mamba Network (GlaTMNet) for precise glacier delineation by integrating global contextual modeling with local feature extraction. Specifically, to overcome the tradeoff between semantic integrity and boundary crispness, GlaTMNet innovates a frequency-aware bidirectional feature fusion strategy. Moving beyond conventional spatial models, it explicitly decouples hierarchical features in the frequency domain. This interactive two-way exchange leverages global semantics to maintain glacier continuity, while using high-frequency details to sharply delineate complex boundaries. Furthermore, to facilitate robust learning of glacier characteristics across diverse regions and satellite sensors, we construct a high-quality, multisource glacier benchmark dataset using Landsat 5/7/8/9 and Sentinel-2 imagery. Extensive experiments on this benchmark dataset demonstrate that GlaTMNet achieves a state-of-the-art mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 97.07%. Compared with existing mainstream deep learning methods, the proposed network exhibits superior segmentation accuracy and robust performance. Notably, GlaTMNet demonstrates remarkable capability in highly complex terrain, effectively mitigating misclassifications induced by terrain shadows and successfully distinguishing glaciers from challenging background classes such as glacial lakes and floating thin ice. Ablation studies quantitatively confirm that incorporating a digital elevation model (DEM) yields a substantial mIoU improvement of 2.48%, particularly in refining ambiguous ice boundaries. Overall, these results highlight GlaTMNet’s strong potential for accurate, large-scale glacier inventories across diverse and challenging mountainous environments.
author: Fawei Kang, Xin Luo, Zhaofeng Deng

title: Multitask Adaptive Quantization for Transformer-Based Remote Sensing Cotraining
content: Deploying Transformer-based remote sensing models jointly trained on scene classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation requires compressing a shared encoder, yet standard quantization-aware training (QAT) is ill-suited for this setting: task-conditioned activations develop incompatible statistical ranges that a single quantization scale cannot serve simultaneously, and the same shared weights carry unequal importance across tasks, causing uniform bit-width assignment to degrade task performance unevenly. We identify task identity as a first-class quantization signal and propose multitask adaptive quantization (MTAQ), a framework that exploits this signal for both activation and weight quantization. For activations, task-specific adaptive correction and scaling (TSACS) corrects task-conditioned activation distributions and applies independent per-task affine quantization, resolving intertask distribution mismatch without duplicating the shared encoder. For weights, task-sensitivity-aware mixed precision (TSMP) allocates bit-widths according to cross-task weight sensitivity, concentrating high precision on shared parameters that are important across tasks. On three remote sensing benchmarks, MTAQ at 4.8-bit average weights and 4-bit activations achieves 95.99% Overall Accuracy (OA), 71.68% mean Average Precision (mAP), and 79.89% mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), closely matching the full-precision RSCoTr baseline; a more aggressive setting with 3.8-bit average weights and 4-bit activations delivers up to  $\mathbf {6.27\times }$  model compression and a  $\mathbf {25.06\times }$  reduction in estimated bit operations (BOPs) relative to the same full-precision RSCoTr baseline, indicating its potential for low-bit onboard remote sensing inference.
author: Shuying Huang, Rongkai Jiang, Yong Yang, Mengmei Zhang, Han Pu

title: MASTrack: Motion–Appearance Semantic Tracking for Thermal Infrared Anti-UAV
content: Infrared anti-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) tracking faces challenges such as tiny targets, weak appearance, complex backgrounds, and rapid motion. Global tracking methods provide strong recovery capability but incur high computational costs, whereas local trackers are prone to drift under fast motion and occlusion. To address these issues, we propose MASTrack, a motion–appearance semantic tracking framework that jointly models visual appearance, historical motion, and target semantics within a local Transformer architecture. Specifically, a Mamba-based motion prompt encoder (MPE) captures long-range dynamics from historical bounding boxes, while a bidirectional motion–appearance decoder (MAD) adaptively integrates motion priors with current visual features. A SeaFormer-based segmenter further generates foreground semantics to reweight classification responses and suppress background interference. Experiments show that MASTrack achieved AUC scores of 72.11%, 64.76%, and 29.57% on the AntiUAV, AntiUAV410, and CSTAntiUAV datasets, respectively, while performing real-time tracking at 100.3 FPS, thereby validating its accuracy, robustness, and efficiency in complex infrared scenarios. Our code will be released on https://github.com/bingbing-wei/MASTrack
author: Bingbing Wei, Xinying Zhang, Xu Wang, Peiwen He, Qingchuan Zhai, Yuanke Zhang

title: A Multitrack InSAR Deformation Field Mosaicking Algorithm Incorporating External GNSS Constraints and a Robust Kalman Filter for Mining Areas
content: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) enables precise deformation mapping and has been widely used in mining areas. However, its limited single-track/frame coverage necessitates multiorbit/frame mosaicking, which introduces inconsistencies in reference frames, viewing geometries, and noise. To address these issues, we have developed a multiorbit deformation field mosaicking algorithm framework. This framework integrates coherence-weighted observations, external GNSS constraints, and a robust Kalman filter. It is specifically designed to enhance robustness in regions characterized by large-gradient deformation and sparse GNSS coverage. Between March 2017 and December 2023, we processed 3852 Sentinel-1 interferograms covering six frames over the northern Shaanxi mining area. The interframe relative observation equation was derived by averaging overlapping regions using coherence weighting. Time series data from GNSS stations were used as absolute constraints, and a leave-one-station-out cross-validation strategy was adopted. In each fold, two stations were used as constraints, while the remaining station was completely withheld for validation. The robust Kalman filter then estimated framewise systematic deviations, yielding a vertically unified deformation field with spatial continuity. Validation against nine overlapping zones and leave-one-station-out GNSS validation demonstrated that the proposed method reduces the root mean square error (RMSE) in overlapping areas by 30.7% and decreases the RMSE and mean absolute error (MAE) relative to GNSS measurements by 30% and 28%, respectively. The 95% confidence intervals were obtained by bootstrap resampling. We further compared the Kalman filter with least-squares adjustment and analyzed the effect of orbital incidence-angle differences on multitrack InSAR, and we discussed the limitations of constant-bias correction. Results show that the Kalman filter preserves the absolute GNSS datum more effectively than least-squares adjustment and mitigates overlap inconsistencies, while pixelwise incidence angles reduce geometry-induced discrepancies. These results confirm the suitability of the framework for large-scale, high-precision deformation monitoring and risk management in mining regions.
author: Shuangcheng Zhang, Jingtao Li, Ning Liu, Zhipeng Ren, Jinzhao Si, Fan Wen, Sijiezi Li, Shuai Gao

title: Theoretical Bounds on Detectability of Tunnel-Induced Subsidence Using SBAS-InSAR
content: Tunnel-induced ground subsidence can progressively compromise overlying infrastructure, making reliable monitoring essential for urban risk management. Although small baseline subset (SBAS)-interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) enables wide-area, millimeter-level deformation monitoring, its ability to detect tunnel-induced settlement is fundamentally limited by interferometric phase noise, coherence, sensor resolution, and tunnel geometry. Existing studies are largely posterior, demonstrating detection after deformation has been observed, with limited capability for a priori feasibility assessment. This article develops a theoretical framework that establishes closed-form detectability limits for tunnel-induced subsidence under SBAS-InSAR. By coupling Peck’s settlement model with a Cramér–Rao bound on interferometric phase variance and the SBAS inversion geometry, analytical expressions are derived for the minimum detectable tunnel length, width, and depth, as well as the maximum detectable depth, as functions of radar wavelength, spatial resolution, coherence, and soil properties. The bounds are evaluated across five radar bands (P, L, S, C, and X) and corroborated through SBAS time-series simulations, which show close agreement with the predicted thresholds. A Sentinel-1 case study over the Dangjin tunnel construction site in South Korea provides a relative, field-based illustration of the coherence-dependent detectability mechanism. The proposed framework delineates the blind zones of SBAS-InSAR and enables a priori assessment of monitoring feasibility, providing a principled basis for sensor selection, acquisition planning, and monitoring-cost optimization.
author: Lakshmi Annamalai, Imran Ahmed Syed, Bishwajit Sharma, Arshad Jamal

title: Reliable Pseudosupervision Construction for Hyperspectral Change Detection via Pseudosample Generation and Robust Representation
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) change detection (HSI-CD) is an important task in Earth observation, identifying land-cover changes from large-scale multitemporal HSIs, which is crucial for Earth science like disaster assessment. However, obtaining a large number of high-quality labeled samples often requires significant manual effort. Therefore, developing effective unsupervised or self-supervised HSI-change detection (CD) methods is of great significance for practical applications. In recent years, significant progress has been made in the construction of self-supervised learning (SSL) paradigms based on pseudolabels and pseudotemporal sample generation, but their performance is still affected by insufficient reliability of supervised signals and limited authenticity of simulated changes. In response to the above issues, this article proposes a reliable pseudosupervised learning method for self-supervised HSI CD (RPSCD). First, the superpixel-assisted Change Mask Module (SACMM) is proposed, which combines coarse-grained change information with SLIC superpixel spatial consistency constraints, and adaptively filters change regions based on change confidence to generate more complete and reliable pseudolabels. Second, the diffusion pseudoimage generation module (DPIGM) is designed, which utilizes high-confidence changed pixels to learn the spectral transfer patterns during the real change process and generates spectral information that is more in line with the actual change characteristics for pseudochange regions through the conditional generation ability of the diffusion model. In addition, a spectral compression module is introduced to reduce redundant information and noise interference in high-dimensional HSI, and is combined with a cross-attention module to enhance the interactive learning ability between bitemporal features. Extensive experiments on three public HSI-CD datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing methods, exhibiting strong robustness and transferability for practical Earth observation.
author: Shuaichen Guo, Dongbo Yu, Lupeng Liu, Ying Wang, Jun Xiao

title: Multispace Distillation-Guided Teacher–Student Framework for Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) aims to automatically identify surface changes by analyzing dual-temporal remote sensing imagery. While recent methods have introduced vision–language models (VLMs) to provide semantic guidance and suppress environment-induced pseudo-changes, they typically rely on direct feature fusion. This often compromises the high-resolution spatial details essential for RSCD or suffers from modality misalignment. A multispace distillation-guided teacher–student (MSD-TS) framework for RSCD is proposed to exploit frozen VLM knowledge through structured textual and visual prototype banks (VPBs), which serve as stable semantic anchors to guide the learning of a change-aware student network (CA-SN). The multispace distillation (MSD)-TS method consists of three key components: a semantic prototype-based teacher network (SPb-TN), the MSD strategy, and a CA-SN. First, the SPb-TN establishes a dual-branch backbone, where the frozen teacher network constructs a textual prototype bank (TPB) and a VPB that serve as structured semantic priors. Then, the MSD strategy bridges the two branches by enforcing the student’s features to align with these teacher-defined prototype banks via multilevel constraints, enabling efficient semantic knowledge transfer. Meanwhile, the CA-SN integrates a difference perception (DP) module and a channel–spatial attention (CSA) module to capture discriminative spatiotemporal changes. Finally, the learned features are fed into the detection module to generate the final detection map. Experimental results on three remote sensing datasets demonstrate that the MSD-TS method outperforms other existing RSCD algorithms.
author: Wuxia Zhang, Xinyi Shi, Hailong Ning, Xueling Chen, Haifeng Zhang, Xiaoqiang Lu

title: Multi-Information Collaborative Correction for Label-Quality-Robust Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
content: Remote sensing image object detection has extensive application value in environmental monitoring, transportation planning, resource management, and military reconnaissance. Most current remote sensing image object detection methods heavily rely on accurate and high-quality labels for training. However, limited by the crowd-sourced labeling process, the nonintuitiveness of remote sensing objects, and the professional requirements for analysis in the remote sensing field, it is often challenging to obtain precise labels. To address this issue, we propose a multi-information collaborative correction-based label-quality-robust object detection (MICC-LROD) model. This model fully leverages category, detail, and spatial information to achieve a high-performance perception of objects in remote sensing images under conditions of low label quality. The model mainly consists of three core components: the category-detail information joint proposal (CDIP) miner, the spatial information-assisted proposal bag (SIPB) optimizer, and an alternating cascading arrangement. Specifically, the CDIP miner can fully capture the detailed features of objects in remote sensing images through its detail information perception branch. Meanwhile, it considers category and detail information during the proposal mining process, obtaining high-quality object proposals. The SIPB optimizer can comprehensively integrate spatial information within a wide receptive field to effectively optimize proposal bags, guaranteeing proposal mining and even the entire label refinement process. Furthermore, we arrange the miner and optimizer in an alternating cascading manner to achieve progressive correction, thereby enhancing adaptability to strongly noisy labels. A series of experimental results demonstrates that the MICC-LROD model can achieve high-performance object detection in remote sensing images with limited label quality of training samples and exhibits excellent adaptability when facing strongly noisy labels.
author: Man Chen, Huaping Zhou, Kelei Sun, Antai Chen

title: SDENet: Synergizing Domain-Adaptive Structural Priors With Edge-Constrained Progressive Decoding for ORSI Salient Object Detection
content: Salient object detection in optical remote sensing imagery (ORSI-SOD) requires accurate region perception and reliable structural recovery. Despite recent advances, existing methods struggle with objects exhibiting strong directional variations, irregular shapes, and large-scale changes, resulting in blurred boundaries and incomplete regions. To address these challenges, we propose SDENet, a unified framework that synergizes domain-adaptive structural priors with edge-constrained progressive decoding for ORSI-SOD. Specifically, domain-adaptive structural priors are constructed through two complementary designs. First, we employ a SAM2 encoder with lightweight gated adapters to enable parameter-efficient transfer of pretrained knowledge to the remote sensing domain. On top of this, we introduce a structural context aggregation (SCA) unit that integrates directional perception with Mamba-based state-space modeling, allowing the model to capture directional cues, multiscale details, and long-range dependencies in a unified manner. The representations learned through these components further give rise to structure-adaptive priors, which provide more reliable guidance for salient object localization and shape recovery. To further improve boundary accuracy and region completeness, we design an edge-constrained progressive decoder that extracts multilevel edge cues and progressively injects them into each decoding stage. By jointly optimizing region reconstruction and boundary preservation, SDENet produces salient maps that achieve more accurate localization, sharper boundaries, and more complete object regions. Extensive experiments on public ORSI-SOD benchmarks (EORSSD, ORSSD, and ORSI-4199) demonstrate that SDENet consistently outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative evaluation and visual quality. The code and results are available at https://github.com/zouduo/SDENet
author: Yuzhao Wang, Duo Zou, Fuming Sun

title: Correction to “UniHyper: A Unified Multimodal Classification Framework for Hyperspectral Images Under Diff-Labeled Scenes”

author: Xiaoyu Tian, Yi Liu, Chuan Fu, Yule Duan, Tan Guo, Fulin Luo

title: Pressure-Aware Temporal Retrieval of Atmospheric Specific Humidity Profiles From FY-3D MWHS-II Observations
content: Atmospheric specific humidity profiles are essential for numerical weather prediction, severe-weather monitoring, and tropical-cyclone analysis. Retrieving humidity profiles from satellite microwave observations remains challenging because the radiance–humidity relationship is nonlinear and the usefulness of preceding local observations varies with pressure level and weather regime. This study develops a pressure-aware temporal retrieval framework for pressure-level specific humidity profiles from Fengyun-3D microwave humidity sounder-II observations and auxiliary environmental variables, using 5G atmospheric reanalysis pressure-level humidity as the supervised reference. Building on forgetting-based temporal attention, the proposed adaptive grouped forgetting Transformer (AGFoX) introduces multiple temporal forgetting prototypes and pressure-aware adaptive fusion. Pressure-level embeddings and sample context generate level-conditioned branch preferences, aggregated into a shared sample-level mixture of grouped-forgetting branches. Experiments use 2021–2025 oceanic Indo-Pacific and western North Pacific data, with 2021–2023 for training, 2024 for validation, and 2025 for independent testing. On the 2025 test set, AGFoX achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.6329 g$\cdot$kg$^{-1}$, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.4748 g$\cdot$kg$^{-1}$, and a correlation coefficient of 0.7394, corresponding to the lowest unweighted RMSE and MAE and the highest correlation coefficient among the compared methods. The improvement is the most evident in the mid-to-upper troposphere. Under moderate-to-strong typhoon conditions, AGFoX shows clearer advantages. Same-collocation comparisons with IGRA radiosonde and COSMIC-2 profiles show reference-dependent results: DNN obtains the lowest aggregate absolute errors against IGRA, whereas AGFoX achieves the lowest aggregate RMSE and MAE and the highest mean levelwise correlation against COSMIC-2 among four compared models.
